Complementarities in behavioral interventions: Evidence from a field experiment on resource conservation
abstract: Behavioral policy often aims at influencing behavior by mitigating biases due to, e.g., imperfect information or inattention. We study how this is affected by the simultaneous presence of multiple biases arising from different sources, through a field experiment on resource conservation in an energy- and water-intensive everyday activity (showering). One intervention, shower energy reports, primarily targeted knowledge about environmental impacts; another intervention, real-time feedback, primarily targeted salience of resource use. We find a striking complementarity. While only the latter induced significant conservation effects when implemented in isolation, each intervention became more effective when implemented jointly. This is consistent with predictions from a theoretical framework that highlights the importance of targeting all relevant sources of bias to achieve behavioral change.
abstract_zh: 行为政策通常旨在通过减轻因信息不完全或注意力不足等原因产生的偏差来影响行为。我们通过一项关于能源和水资源密集型日常活动（淋浴）中资源节约的田野实验，研究多种来源的偏差同时存在时，这一过程会受到怎样的影响。其中一种干预为淋浴能耗报告，主要针对环境影响方面的知识；另一种干预为实时反馈，主要针对资源使用的显著性（salience）。我们发现了显著的互补性。单独实施时只有后者能产生显著的节约效果，而两种干预联合实施时，每一种都变得更为有效。这与一个理论框架的预测一致，该框架强调了针对所有相关偏差来源以实现行为改变的重要性。

Motivating household water conservation: A field experiment in Singapore
abstract: We test and compare different incentives in motivating water conservation using a randomized controlled trial. In a field experiment carried out with Singaporean households, regular feedback was given, with informative, normative and monetary incentives provided to different groups. Evidence shows that all households saved an average of 4 Litres of water per person per day, with no difference in treatment effect found across various groups. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the water saving effect is also found to be more significant with high baseline users, who saved up to 5.9 Litres per person per day. High baseline households also respond more positively to the non-monetary incentives.
abstract_zh: 我们利用随机对照试验，检验并比较了激励家庭节水的不同方式。在一项与新加坡家庭合作开展的田野实验中，我们定期向家庭提供反馈，并向不同组别提供信息型、规范型和货币型激励。证据表明，所有家庭人均每日平均节水4升，且不同组别之间的处理效应没有差异。或许并不令人意外的是，基线用水量较高的家庭节水效果更为显著，人均每日节水可达5.9升。基线用水量较高的家庭对非货币激励的反应也更为积极。
